You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications Summary

#### File Modifications
1. **File: `core/src/main/java/org/apache/accumulo/core/util/shell/Shell.java`**
   - **Line Changed**: The format of the string used to append the authorization timeout display has been modified.
   - **Modification**: 
     - The original code used `String.format("%.2fs%n", TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS.toSeconds(authTimeout))` which formats the authorization timeout as a floating-point number with two decimal places.
     - This was changed to `String.format("%ds%n", TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS.toSeconds(authTimeout))`, which formats the authorization timeout as a decimal integer without any decimal places.

#### Relationships
- The change in the `Shell.java` file is aimed at improving the representation of the authorization timeout by formatting it as a whole number (seconds) instead of as a floating-point number. This enhances the clarity and correctness of how the timeout duration is displayed to users, aligning with the intended use case where a decimal is unnecessary for whole seconds representation.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
sb.append("- Authorization timeout: ").append(String.format("%.2fs%n", TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS.toSeconds(authTimeout)));
```
Reason:
The use of `String.format("%.2fs%n", ...)` formats the authorization timeout as a floating-point number with two decimal places, which can mislead users into thinking the timeout includes fractional seconds, even when it is a whole number.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
sb.append("- Authorization timeout: ").append(String.format("%ds%n", TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS.toSeconds(authTimeout)));
```
Reason:
The change to `String.format("%ds%n", ...)` formats the authorization timeout as an integer, clearly representing the timeout duration in whole seconds without implying any fractional values, thus providing a more accurate and user-friendly display.
